title: Octopuses
passages: An octopus can change the colour of its skin in less than a second. Its skin holds thousands of tiny sacs of colour called CHROMATOPHORES. Each sac is ringed by small muscles. When the muscles pull, the sac stretches open and the colour spreads, like ink on wet paper. Some octopuses can also change the texture of their skin, raising little bumps and ridges so they look like rock or coral. They use these changes for CAMOUFLAGE, to warn rivals, and perhaps even to show how they feel.

Octopuses are also clever problem solvers. In aquariums, they have learned to twist the lids off jars to reach a crab inside. With no bones in their bodies, they can squeeze through almost any gap wider than their hard beak. Many hide in dens made of rocks or empty shells, and some even carry coconut shells or clam shells with them as portable shelters. If a PREDATOR comes close, an octopus can squirt a dark cloud of ink and jet away. Its eight arms hold about two thirds of its NEURONS, so each arm can taste, touch and act almost on its own.
